content.text: A custom Hook is a way to reuse code, not a place to keep data. Every component that calls it gets its own copy of the state inside, exactly as if it had called
itself. When two components need the same data, the state has to live in one place, like a common parent, a context or an external store, and the Hook can be how they read it.

It's a reasonable guess. The Hook lives in one module, and a JavaScript module is loaded once, so it feels like whatever is inside gets created once too. The name helps:

Sharing means one copy with one owner. React's docs call this a single source of truth, and the usual move is

: put the state in the closest common parent and pass it down as props. When that parent is far above, pass it through context, as above. When the data already lives outside React, like the browser's online status or a state library's store,

content.text: The third row surprises people most. A

Hook that fetches in an Effect, called from the page, the sidebar and the header, sends the same request three times and keeps three copies of the result, which can disagree for a moment. Fetch once in a parent and pass the result down, or use a data library that caches by key.

blocks.title: A module variable isn't shared state

content.text: Moving the array to the top of the module, as

, does make it shared, but React has no idea when it changes, so no component re-renders. And when you render on a server, that one variable is shared by every request, so one user's cart can leak into another user's page.

blocks.title: The Hook runs on every render of its caller

content.text: A custom Hook's code re-runs whenever the component that calls it re-renders, so it always sees the latest props and state. That also means it has to stay pure, like the component body it's part of.
How to apply it in your project

content.text: read the context instead of owning the state, and throw a clear error when it's called outside the provider, so a missing provider fails loudly instead of silently showing an empty cart.

items.title: Count the Effects in shared Hooks

content.text: A Hook with a fetch or a subscription runs it once per caller. If three components need the same data, fetch it once above them and pass it down.

items.text: A custom Hook reuses code: every call gets its own state, refs and Effects, as if they were written in the caller.
Two components calling the same Hook see the same data only when the Hook reads it from one shared place.
To share state, lift it to a common parent, provide it through context or subscribe to an external store, and let the Hook hide which one.
A module-level variable isn't a fix: React won't re-render when it changes, and on a server every request shares it.
